name: Behavioral Intervention & Nudge Strategies
description: Selecting and implementing behavioral strategies: defaulting, educational nudges, habit disruption, automation, choice architecture framing, and constructive friction.

subskills.name: Educational Framing & Encouragement Nudges
subskills.description: Using informative framing, micro-copy, and timely encouragement to guide user action.

subskills.name: Defaulting & Opt-In/Opt-Out Architecture
subskills.description: Setting smart, ethical pre-selected defaults to harness status quo bias.

subskills.name: Choice Architecture & Decoy Effects
subskills.description: Structuring option sets, decoy effects, tier pricing tables, and reducing choice overload.

subskills.name: Reflective Prompting & Cognitive Pauses
subskills.description: Injecting prompts that encourage users to consciously evaluate options before committing.

subskills.name: Incidental Action Pairing & Piggybacking
subskills.description: Attaching the desired target behavior to an action the user is already routinely performing.

subskills.name: Automation & Recurring Rules
subskills.description: Automating recurring behaviors (auto-invest, recurring orders, background sync).

subskills.name: Habit Disruption & Friction Insertion
subskills.description: Breaking unwanted automatic routines by introducing physical or cognitive friction.

subskills.name: Systemic Habit Ecosystems & Long-Term Retention
subskills.description: Designing multi-touchpoint behavioral feedback loops that sustain long-term engagement across lifecycles.

subskills.name: Constructive Friction & High-Stakes Decision UX
subskills.description: Strategically introducing constructive friction for high-stakes decisions (security, financial confirmation, data deletion).
